summary: Two range lights on the western arm of Sydney Harbour, Cape Breton: 1905 wooden towers, rebuilt in 2008-2010, and a new line of towers in 2024. Closed to visitors.

structures.note: Fixed white catoptric light, 58 ft above high water in 1905; lantern of red polygonal iron
Replica of the 1905 tower built by DFO, original iron lantern refurbished and reused; inactive since 2024
White daymark with red vertical stripe; fixed green
Square in plan, square wooden lantern, painted white; 120 ft above high water in 1905
Replaced the 1905 wooden tower; Lighthouse Directory gives 2008, Lighthouse Friends 2009
Occulting green, 9 s light and 1 s eclipse; Lighthouse Directory describes the 2024 rear as octagonal pyramidal

access.note: Site and tower closed; the Lighthouse Directory calls the site private property. Keep off the point; do not climb the towers.

events.note: Front and rear range towers erected near Dixon Point, on the south side of the west arm of Sydney Harbour
Both lights put in operation at the opening of navigation, 1905
A fourth-order lens with an occulting screen provided for the front light
Front light changed from fixed white to revolving white (Lighthouse Friends; the 1908 report gives only the lens and screen)
Roy Lewis's post changed to caretaker when the lights were fully automated (Lighthouse Friends). The NSLPS says automated by 1993.
Red bands on the range towers changed from horizontal to vertical
Rear 1905 wooden tower replaced by a skeletal tower (Lighthouse Directory: 2008; Lighthouse Friends: 2009)
Front tower, found badly rotten, rebuilt as a replica of the 1905 structure; original iron lantern refurbished and placed on top
Range line changed and new towers required; the 2026 Coast Guard list gives the new positions
New front and rear range towers, each 9.0 m (skeleton)

corrections.why: The record's point is the pre-2024 front tower (NSLPS gives 46 10 48.6 N, 60 15 00.7 W for the old tower). The 2026 Coast Guard list places the new front light at 46 10 39.7 N, 060 15 30.0 W.
Rear light, entry 783 on the 2026 Coast Guard list: 46 09 11.6 N, 060 17 01.5 W. The record's point is the old rear site.
The 2026 list shows the rebuilt front light as fixed green (F G). The F Y of the 2010 replica is no longer shown.
The 2026 list gives the new front light's focal height as 23.8 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record says sources differ on whether the light is still lit. The 2026 Coast Guard list shows both new range lights operating 24 hours; what is no longer lit is the 2010 replica front tower, inactive since 2024.
The record's position is the pre-2024 front tower. The 2024 range was set on a new line (Lighthouse Directory), and the 2026 list gives the new positions.

The Directory calls the front site and tower closed and private property, and says the rear site appears open with the tower closed. Lighthouse Friends says the grounds and tower of both are closed. The story gives all three.
The 2026 Coast Guard list gives the rear light focal height as 60.2 m; the Directory gives the focal plane as 37 m (121 ft). Both are stated; not resolved.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-28 (page images read on archive.org). 1906 report printed p.30 (scan 35): 'The tower is 53 feet high from its base to the vane on the lantern' is clean on the page image, so the report gives 53 ft and the Lighthouse Friends figure of 63 ft is its own disagreement; the story states all three heights. 1911 report printed p.258 (scan 260): 'Sydney Range Fr | J. B. Rudderham | Jan. 15, 1905 | 300' confirmed; the back-light row prints the name as 'B. A. J. Lewis' (station: ditto 'B.'), 22 May 1905, $180; the story says so. 1907 report printed p.174 (scan 183): 'Rudderham, S. | Sydney Range Front Light | Jan. 15, 1905 | 250 00' confirmed. 1908 report printed p.146 (scan 153): 'Rudderham, S. | Sydney Range Front Light | Jan. 15, 1905 | 250 00' confirmed. Both 1907 and 1908 pay $250, which matches LF's first salary; the story does not state these pay figures because the cached OCR does not place the salary beside the name, so the evidence cannot be quoted. A reviewer may add the $250 with the image as the source. 1908 report (printed 1907): the 'fourth order lens with an occulting screen' passage is on p.51 as cited but the page was not checked on the image; the report's year covers the work to 31 March 1907, so the story does not give a year from the report itself and cites LF for 1907. CCG list p.106 entries 782 and 783 read in the cached text (both 'Year round'; 782 F G 23.8, 9.0 m square skeleton tower, white daymark with red vertical stripe; 783 Oc G 10s 60.2, Flash 9 s / eclipse 1 s, bearing 216 35 and 3352.8 m); the page number was not checked on the image. Front tower location: the Department says near Dixon Point; LF says near Point Edward; both are stated. Not stated: the rear tower shape (CCG: square skeleton; Directory: octagonal pyramidal); the 2010 replica being DFO work (LF, NSLPS) versus Coast Guard (Directory); the IAAC assessment describes a 40 ft steel front tower and a 30 ft rear, an earlier design than the 2026 list's 9.0 m towers. Roster after 1910 (Howard Lewis, Gordon Rudderham, Andrew Musgrave, G. Rose, W. Daley, Roy Lewis) comes from LF only and is marked as unchecked in the story. Automation: LF 1965 (Roy Lewis to caretaker) vs NSLPS by 1993, stated. NSLPS 'Fixed Yellow (1992)' and LF's isophase yellow after 2010 are not used. No storm, wreck or rescue for these lights in the Canadian reports read or in LF/Directory: the storms chapter is omitted, as the research says.
